title: An abelian inclusion retracts up to a positive integer
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A/k$ and $B/k$ be abelian varieties [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $i:B\hookrightarrow A$ be a closed immersion of $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. There exist an integer $n>0$ and a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism $r:A\to B$ such that $r\circ i=[n]_B$, with multiplication as in [def-sc-mult-n].

source.place: Proposition 8.23, printed pp.152–153, with G=A and its abelian subvariety B; normalize by translation and use 8.19, as in the proof of Theorem 8.24. This is the multiple-retraction input, not the complement conclusion.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A$ and $B$ are geometrically integral; they are smooth, proper (hence separated and of finite type) and connected by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. They are commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative]. Thus [lem-sfb-smooth-commutative-subgroup-quotient] applies to $i$ and gives $p:A\to Q$ with the stated torsor identity. Choose a nonempty affine open $S=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Q$. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, the field of fractions of the domain $R$. Its spectrum is the generic point of $S$. The pullback $V=A\times_Q\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a torsor under $B_K$.

source.place: Proposition 8.23, first three sentences of proof, p.153; Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.27.

proof.text: The group scheme $B_K$ is an abelian variety by [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], hence smooth, separated and of finite type and geometrically integral by [def-sc-abelian-variety, lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], and commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative]. Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-torsor-positive-weight] over $K$ to obtain $n>0$ and $\phi_\eta:V\to B_K$ with $\phi_\eta(v+b)=\phi_\eta(v)+[n]b$ as morphisms. Positivity is part of this input: no inversion of $n$ in $k$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 8.22 and its use in Proposition 8.23, pp.152–153.

proof.text: Index the principal opens $D(f)\subseteq S$ by nonzero $f\in R$, ordered by reverse inclusion; intersections $D(fg)$ make this a directed system with affine transitions and limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$ (on rings the union of the localizations $R_f$ is $K$). The models $A\times_QS$ and $B\times_kS$ are of finite presentation over $S$: the first is a base change of $p$, and for the second smoothness gives local finite presentation and properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) to spread $\phi_\eta$ to $\phi_U:A\times_QU\to B\times_kU$ for some nonempty principal open $U\subseteq S$. The two equivariance composites from $(A\times_QU)\times_kB$ to $B\times_kU$ are morphisms of finite-presentation $U$-schemes and agree over $K$. Clause (3) of the same spreading theorem, shrinking $U$ once more, makes them equal over $U$. Since $p$ is surjective and $A$ integral, $p^{-1}(U)$ is a nonempty dense open of $A$. Projecting $\phi_U$ to $B$ gives an equivariant morphism $\psi:p^{-1}(U)\to B$.

source.place: Proposition 8.23, extension of the generic-fibre map to a rational map; expanded using Stacks limits.tex, Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (2),(3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-weil-extension-to-abelian-variety] to extend $\psi$ to $\phi:A\to B$. Compare on $A\times_kB$ the morphisms $(a,b)\mapsto\phi(a+i(b))$ and $(a,b)\mapsto\phi(a)+[n]b$. They agree on $p^{-1}(U)\times_kB$, since $p(a+i(b))=p(a)$. The product is an abelian variety by [lem-sfb-abelian-finite-product], hence integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]. The open is nonempty (it contains the image of $p^{-1}(U)$ under $a\mapsto(a,0)$), hence dense. It is scheme-theoretically dense: restriction from any affine-domain coordinate ring to a nonempty open is injective, since restriction further to a principal open $D(f)$ is the injective localization $R\to R_f$. Thus [lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open], with separated target $B$, gives $\phi(a+i(b))=\phi(a)+[n]b$ globally as morphisms.

source.place: Proposition 8.23, last two sentences, p.153; extension by 8.18, and the dense-open equality argument.

proof.text: Put $c=\phi(0_A)\in B(k)$ and define the regular $k$-map $r(a)=\phi(a)-c$, using the group inverse, addition and the constant map with value $c$ from [def-sc-group-scheme]. Then $r(0_A)=0_B$, and substituting $(0_A,b)$ into the preceding morphism identity gives $r(i(b))=[n]_B(b)$. This substitution is a pullback along the morphism $B\to A\times_kB$, $b\mapsto(0_A,b)$, so the result is an equality of scheme morphisms, not merely on $k$-points.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 8.24, first paragraph: translation of the map of Proposition 8.23, p.153.

proof.text: To check the homomorphism condition, form the morphism $d:A\times_kA\to B$ defined by $d(x,y)=r(x+y)-r(x)-r(y)$, using the group operations of [def-sc-group-scheme] and commutativity [lem-sc-av-commutative]. It is identically zero on $A\times\{0_A\}$. The first factor $A$ is proper, geometrically connected and geometrically reduced by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]; the second is connected, and $B$ is separated and of finite type by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Therefore [lem-sc-rigidity] gives $d=g\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$. Pullback along $y\mapsto(0_A,y)$ gives $g(y)=r(y)-r(0_A)-r(y)=0$. Hence $d=0$, so $r$ preserves addition. Together with $r(0_A)=0_B$ this makes $r$ a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism, with $r\circ i=[n]_B$ as already proved.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q103-20c0c550c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the three new nodes and every cited statement in full. I checked them against Milne, Algebraic Groups (iAG2017): 8.16-8.19, Lemma 8.22 with its proof, Prop 8.23 with its proof and Thm 8.24's proof (pp.152-153), plus 5.14, 5.27 and 1.63. The six steps follow 8.23 in order (quotient, generic-fibre torsor, 8.22 averaging, spreading by 01ZM clauses (2)/(3), extension by 8.18, equality on a scheme-theoretically dense open), then add the 8.24 normalization and 8.19 homomorphy via lem-sc-rigidity with y0=0. n>0 is correct: 8.22's proof uses n=1 or the degree of a separable residue field. The statement is unchanged and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live. No repair note exists, so the re-split rule does not apply. The new nodes are all true, statement-only, self-contained and smaller than the item. Torsor averaging holds because V is smooth by fpqc descent and the Galois-invariant sum descends; it allows p|n and has no rational point. The smooth commutative quotient holds by reducedness descent, the smooth kernel and geometric irreducibility; edge cases H=0 and H=G are fine. The Weil extension to an abelian target holds for any field, with uniqueness from a separated target and a reduced source. I searched for duplicates with rg -L over the snapshot, live and side-live and found none; the new ids do not collide. Accepted tool uses: thm-pd-spreading-out, lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence and lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open. lem-sc-rigidity is Lean-closed per lean_audit and used as a black box; it is not declared in tool_uses, and the maintainer may record it. review_split.py gave 'no such node' for every citation inside the snapshot because of symlinked chapter directories; I verified by hand that every id exists. No fixes.
